💡 budget-tracker-tui | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: Tracking personal finances and gaining insights into spending habits through a terminal interface.
✨ Key Features: • Add, edit, delete, filter, and sort income and expense transactions • Recurring transactions with optional forecasting • Hierarchical categories and subcategories with fuzzy search • Monthly and category summaries with interactive charts • Monthly and per-category budgets
📖 Summary: Budget Tracker TUI is a terminal-based application built with Rust that allows users to track personal income and expenses. It provides features for managing transactions, visualizing financial data through charts and summaries, and setting budgets.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 GPU-Share | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To create a private, secure, and distributed network for running Dockerized GPU workloads among trusted peers, leveraging idle GPU resources without external cloud dependencies.
✨ Key Features: • Authenticated peer-to-peer connections for Docker GPU jobs • No SSH, VPN, or cloud infrastructure required • Default-deny allowlist for security • Jobs run within containers • Mutual pairing with signed codes
📖 Summary: GPUMesh enables secure, peer-to-peer sharing of Docker GPU jobs among trusted users without relying on centralized cloud services or complex network configurations like SSH or VPNs. It facilitates turning idle NVIDIA GPUs into a private, distributed compute network.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 tuitter | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Interacting with X (Twitter) content directly from the command line interface.
✨ Key Features: • Terminal UI client for X (Twitter) • Authentication with X account • Browse and interact with content • Built with TypeScript and OpenTUI • Optional screen-time limit with daily tracking
📖 Summary: tuitter is a terminal UI client for X (Twitter) built with TypeScript and OpenTUI. It allows users to authenticate with their X account and interact with content directly from their terminal.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 caesium-app-web | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Compressing images offline and in-browser for privacy and efficiency.
✨ Key Features: • JPG, PNG and WebP supported • Lossy and lossless compression • Keeps images metadata • Before/after comparison • Runs entirely on your browser, no images are uploaded or processed on any external server
📖 Summary: Caesium Web Image Compressor is a privacy-focused, offline web application that allows users to compress JPG, PNG, and WebP images directly in their browser. It supports both lossy and lossless compression, preserves image metadata, and offers a before/after comparison feature, ensuring no images are uploaded or processed on external servers.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
